column1: # Swahili (sw) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#                                 the language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n/mod.rs)
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Standard Swahili (Kiswahili Sanifu) computing and photo-editing vocabulary (safu, brashi, uteuzi,
# turubai, barakoa ...) in the neutral register of East African software. No proprietary
# localisation resource, string table or product UI was consulted or copied; add entries the same
# way. Menu commands use the imperative (Fungua, Hifadhi kama…). Product and technology names
# (PhotoCraft, Photoshop, PSD, OpenType, CMYK, RGB, Lab ...) stay as they are, as do key names,
# units and placeholders; the trailing "…" of dialog commands and trailing colons are kept.
# Swahili plural rule (CLDR): one|other, one is n = 1; the counted noun changes class prefix where
# it has one (kitendo 1 / vitendo 3) and keeps its form in the N class (safu 1 / safu 3).
# Machine-translated with Claude (Anthropic) for @tronicum; not yet reviewed by a native speaker.
